note: The canonical bias survey, with three taxonomies covering metrics, datasets and mitigation stages.
title: Bias and Fairness in Large Language Models: A Survey
explain_beginner: Large language models are powerful AI systems that generate human-like text, but they can inadvertently learn and spread unfair biases from their training data. This survey examines how to identify these biases and fix them. The authors created three organizational frameworks covering how to measure bias, what test datasets exist to catch it, and what techniques can reduce it at different stages of model development. Understanding these problems matters because these systems increasingly influence important decisions affecting real people's lives.
explain_business: Organizations deploying large language models face risks from embedded social biases that can harm users and create legal exposure. This survey provides a structured framework for understanding bias problems and solutions across the entire model lifecycle. Decision makers should use these taxonomies to evaluate which mitigation strategies fit their development stage and risk tolerance. The consolidated datasets enable systematic testing before deployment. Understanding these categorized approaches helps organizations implement fairness as a technical requirement alongside performance metrics, reducing reputational damage and ensuring systems treat all users equitably.
explain_practitioner: This comprehensive survey consolidates bias evaluation and mitigation approaches for large language models through three taxonomies. The evaluation metrics taxonomy organizes assessment methods by operational level: embeddings, probability distributions, and text generation. The dataset taxonomy categorizes bias testing resources by structure and targeted harms while providing consolidated access to public benchmarks. The mitigation taxonomy classifies intervention techniques across four stages: preprocessing, in-training, intra-processing, and post-processing, with detailed subcategories. The work synthesizes recent research to clarify methodological relationships and identify research directions for reducing harmful bias propagation in language models.
